page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Orthoboric acid is formed
lines: Borax is the salt of the weak acid
H₃BO₃, and sulphuric acid is stronger,
On warming and then cooling, white
crystals of orthoboric acid separate out
and sodium sulphate stays in solution.
steps.why: A stronger acid displaces a weaker one from its salt, and boric acid is only sparingly soluble in cold water, so it is the solid that appears while the sodium sulphate remains dissolved.
common_mistakes: Naming metaboric acid HBO₂ as the product. HBO₂ forms when boric acid itself is heated to 370 K, not in this reaction.
Saying sodium sulphate crystallises out. Boric acid is the sparingly soluble one, so it is what separates on cooling.
steps.memory_tip: The stronger acid goes in, the weaker acid comes out: H₂SO₄ in, H₃BO₃ out.
steps.margin_note: Say that the crystals appear on cooling. Boric acid is sparingly soluble in cold water.

steps.label: Balanced equation
lines: Borax has four boron atoms, so four
molecules of boric acid are formed.
Borax is the decahydrate, so its ten
water molecules are written in. Five of
them react and five are left over.
steps.why: One formula unit of borax carries four boron atoms, so four molecules of boric acid come out. Writing borax as Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O keeps the water of crystallisation in the equation: five of those ten water molecules supply the hydrogen and oxygen the four boric acid molecules need, and the other five are left over on the right.
common_mistakes: Writing a single H₃BO₃ on the right. Four boron atoms give four molecules of boric acid.
Leaving the 5H₂O off the right side, which leaves both hydrogen and oxygen unbalanced.
steps.memory_tip: Four borons go in, so four molecules of boric acid come out.
steps.margin_note: Check the hydrogen too: 20 + 2 = 22 on the left and 12 + 10 = 22 on the right.

insider_note: Name the product — orthoboric acid, also called boric acid — and then write the balanced equation; the two together are the complete answer.
